new_written_results.statement: -123*c/2 <= Z(R) <= Gamma(R)+69*c, for every real R>=1. Gamma(R) denotes Gamma_(1/3)(log R).
new_written_results.proof: Write B=D+P+Q+A. The paid-sector bounds give -69*c<=B<=123*c/2 and Gamma=Z+B>=0.
Substitute V(x)=int_1^x M(v)*v^(-3/2)dv in the literal dyadic filter. Endpoints are unchanged; equivalently use continuous compact atom partial summation.

new_written_results.premises: MertensLogSquareBound: abs(M(v))<=3*v/log(v)^2 for v>1. Published mathematics, not a native Lean supplier.
new_written_results.statement: For R>=16: Z(R)<=69*c+216/25+81*(1-2^(-1/2))^2*int_(log16)^(log R) exp(t/3)/(t-log4)^4 dt. This bound is NOT uniform.
new_written_results.proof: SC2 gives abs(L(x))<=9*(1-2^(-1/2))*sqrt(x)/log(x/4)^2. For startup, ell_n<=3/(5sqrt(n)) and sum_(n<=x)n^(-1/2)<=2sqrt(x) give Gamma(16)<216/25. Square the complete signed reading and integrate; do not split core signs.

Set u=t-log4. On u>=24 the derivative of exp(u/3)/u^4 is at least one sixth of that function. The remaining compact integral is <=exp(8)/(3log(4)^3). The growing term tends to infinity, so this does not prove (*).

new_written_results.premises: Reported external ZF_7/8 plus the existing written, source-exact contour transfer.
new_written_results.statement: For 3/8<sigma<=1/2 and R>=1: Z(R)<=69*c+8*B_sigma*R^(2*(sigma-1/3)), with B_sigma exactly as in the bound source guide. At sigma=2/5 the extra term is (42592/(9*pi))*exp(2400+1440^90)*R^(2/15).
new_written_results.proof: Finite weight comparison gives H_(1/3)(log R)<=R^(2*(sigma-1/3))*H_sigma(log R). Apply Gamma_(1/3)<=8H_(1/3) and SC1. No new contour or coefficient bridge. The exponent cannot be removed.

new_written_results.premises: Only the written finite atom/sector estimates, no Mertens decay or zero-free input.
new_written_results.statement: For S>=R>=4, abs(B(S)-B(R))<=eta(R)=c*((25/2)*(4/R)^(2/3)+89*(4/R)^(1/6)). Thus B has a finite limit, and Z either has a finite real limit or tends to positive infinity.
new_written_results.proof: Only smaller indices m>R/4 have future Gram mass. Diagonal and divisible-ray tails cost (5/2+10)c*(4/R)^(2/3). Short gaps cost 14c*(4/R)^(1/6). Split large-gcd coordinates a at sqrt(R/4): their tails cost (15+60)c*(4/R)^(1/6). Since Gamma is nondecreasing and Z=Gamma-B, the dichotomy follows.

new_written_results.statement: Its validity would exclude actual zeta zeros with Re(s)>=5/6, including the boundary. This is a necessary condition, not a new zero-free theorem.
new_written_results.proof: The actual damped local reading would belong to L2. Its Laplace transform is bounded by norm(f)/sqrt(2epsilon) at z=1/3+epsilon+i*gamma. Its initial transform equals (1-2^(-z))*(1-2^(-z-1/2))/(z*(z+1/2)*zeta(z+1/2)); the numerator has no zeros for Re(z)>0. Analytic uniqueness excludes interior poles. A boundary zeta zero of multiplicity r>=1 would force epsilon^(-r), contradicting the L2 epsilon^(-1/2) bound.
